summary.headline: Crompton Q1 FY27 revenue rose 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore and EBITDA margin expanded 20 bps to 10%, despite roughly Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 11.8% YoY to Rs 2,235 crore, with EBITDA up 14.2% to Rs 224 crore and PAT up 15.2% to Rs 143 crore. Management attributed the quarter to commodity cost and availability disruptions, which led to about Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mainly in fans and partly in lighting. Pricing actions of high-single to low-double digits covered about 80% of inflation. Management said supply constraints were largely resolved by end-June and Q2 has started well.

financial_highlights.value: +10.6% YoY (ECD revenue not stated in absolute terms)
financial_highlights.change: Management cited ~12% growth on the Rs 200 crore supply-loss basis
+14% YoY; EBIT +19.5% YoY; +18% excluding internal mixer grinder sales to Crompton
Five new BLDC fans launched in the quarter

segments.name: ECD (Electrical Consumer Durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue +10.6% YoY; BLDC portfolio grew ~45%; market leader in ceiling fans with share gains; pumps gained share; domestic appliances grew double digits led by water heaters, which now lead General Trade in volume. Management cited ~Rs 200 crore of lost primary sales, mostly fans.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 269 crore, +15.4% YoY, on B2B and B2C growth; EBIT margin 12%. B2C margins expanded while B2B margins contracted because of pre-contracted prices.

segments.name: Butterfly Gandhimathi Appliances
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 214 crore, +14% YoY; EBIT +19.5% with margin 4.2%. Growth +18% excluding internal mixer-grinder sales to Crompton; share gains in mixer grinders, pressure cookers and glass tops.

segments.name: Solar rooftops and solar pumps (renewables)
segments.commentary: Rooftop order book about Rs 500 crore, of which about Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months, mainly Andhra Pradesh (~38,000 rooftops for SC/ST homes). Revenue recognised on installation, expected to pick up in Q2; EBITDA margin said to be similar to company EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: A&P as a percentage of sales over the year expected to be similar to last year, per management.
Q2 started well; management is optimistic as volatility has settled.
Solar rooftop order book expected to see the bulk of execution in Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Management does not give formal forward guidance; no price increases seen as necessary at present, with cost measures and operating leverage expected to help margins.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore including a large warehouse; otherwise regular capex trends to continue.
Brand launch event on 18 August 2026 and capital markets investor event on 20 August 2026.
capex_capacity: Baddi plant capacity was raised by about 50% at a very low investment of about Rs 50 lakh, per management.
Greenfield manufacturing plant planned over the next 2-3 years at about Rs 350 crore, including a large warehousing unit.
No plan currently to manufacture wires; wires are sourced via outsourced manufacturing.
Wires business launched in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, present in about 14 towns and cities.
demand_pricing: Pricing actions of high-single digits to low-double digits taken across segments, covering about 80% of inflationary pressure; management said the market has accepted them.
Management attributed Q1 slowdown to supply disruption (~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales, mostly fans, also some lighting) and price-induced sticker shock, not demand suppression.
Butterfly core categories grew in line with competition; core channels grew above 20%; induction cooktops not a significant contributor yet. Gas cylinder shortages hit gas stove sales in the quarter.
Management said channel inventory is not a concern; some replenishment from other sources expected.
Competitors did not follow with the same pricing, per management, possibly due to low-cost inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Was volume growth in ECD modest given the price increases, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said supply disruptions cost about Rs 200 crore or more of sales; the company runs a lean inventory model and prioritised revenue maximisation within available supply.

qa_highlights.question: Will A&P and other expenses normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P is an active investment year for the Crompton brand; management expects A&P as a percentage of sales over the year to be similar to last year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar rooftop order book, execution and payment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 500 crore order book with Rs 450 crore to execute over 6-8 months; government pays 40% upfront on product demonstration, with the balance on installation. B2C solar rooftop revenue has started.

qa_highlights.question: Would the Rs 200 crore loss come back?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a mix; some channel replenishment will occur, but Crompton expects to claw back share as supply normalises. CFO said some Q1 impact is seasonal and will not recover quarter-on-quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further price hikes needed given copper costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no sharp set of additional price increases appears necessary currently; cost measures and operating leverage should help. For solar, panel prices are falling and the company's scale improves negotiation.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of Butterfly growth vs competitor TTK's 34%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core category business (about 85% of Butterfly turnover) grew in line with competition; induction cooktops were not a major contributor, and gas stove sales were hit by LPG cylinder shortages.

risks_watch: Recovery of the ~Rs 200 crore lost primary sales and sustainability of supply after the June-end stabilisation.
Copper and other commodity costs remain high; competitors have not matched price increases, which may lead to share shifts or later pressure.
Solar rooftop revenue depends on installation timing (recognised on installation); the Q1 execution gap may extend into Q2.
Solar pumps payment delays from government were seen earlier but reportedly improved; monsoon can delay installations.
Butterfly's EBIT margin of 4.2% is thin; competitive intensity in kitchen appliances is high.
Lighting B2B margins contracted due to pre-contracted prices.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and Q2 momentum, but defensive when probed on the Rs 200 crore lost sales and channel inventory. Management deflected segment and sub-segment detail, repeatedly citing non-disclosure.
